verdict.rationale: Ramp ships a full OpenAPI schema, machine-readable llms.txt docs, and even a dedicated 'Developer MCP' server that lets AI assistants query/search/read the API reference and schemas live (developer_docs_search/schema/read tools), plus a sandbox environment (demo-api.ramp.com) where API calls can actually be executed without real money movement — together these approximate an AI-native, queryable/interactive reference with runnable calls. However there's no evidence of a traditional interactive API-reference UI (e.g., Swagger/Redoc try-it-out console) with clickable runnable examples in a browser. Missing for 10: a dedicated interactive/try-it-out API console in docs, explicit runnable code snippets tied to the reference, independent confirmation of the sandbox being usable end-to-end for reference examples.
